items.author: Giovann35084111
items.context: Giovanni (Scientific Bitcoin Institute): hacia 2017 las transacciones on-chain, que crecían según un power law con exponente cercano a 4, se frenaron, y la volatilidad de la pendiente diaria del power law de precio se duplicó. Hipótesis: derivados, custodios y «paper Bitcoin» sacaron actividad de la cadena mientras precio y adopción siguieron su escala.
items.suggested_text: Interesting overlap. If custodians and derivatives pulled activity off-chain after 2017, on-chain tx would understate adoption while price kept its trend. How do you separate that from fees pushing small payments off-chain? My notes: https://x.com/forecastquant/status/2118779927340470279

items.author: 0xLofty
items.context: 0xLofty afirma que esta caída es «el dump final del ciclo» y traza el camino $74K → $72K → $69K → $65K → piso final; dice haber acertado piso y techo en ciclos anteriores y pide guardar el gráfico.
items.suggested_text: Four levels and one direction is a clean plan, but what invalidates it? Without a line where the call is wrong, it's hard to compare in a few weeks. I'd rather hold spot with no leverage than bet on $BTC tagging $65K exactly.

items.author: CryptoNobler
items.context: CryptoNobler (cita a 0xLofty): una ballena de la era Satoshi habría «vendido» 7.650 BTC (~$565M) tras 15 años de holdeo, y lo lee como señal de que viene otra caída fuerte.
items.suggested_text: Coins moving after 15 years isn't automatically a sale. Has anyone confirmed they hit an exchange, or is it a wallet move? An old holder upgrading custody looks almost identical on-chain, so I'd wait before reading it as a $BTC crash signal.
